title: Delegating performance of a duty
summary: Delegation arranges for someone else to perform a contractual duty. It must be distinguished from transferring the right to receive performance and from releasing the original obligor.
notes:
Identify who originally owed the duty, what performance was promised, and whether the obligee has an important interest in that particular person’s performance. Personal skill, trust, contractual restrictions, and the governing law may matter. A transfer of performance responsibilities does not automatically prove that the original party was discharged; that is a separate question about the agreement and any substitution accepted by the obligee.

The assigned pages introduce delegation. Their scope should not be mistaken for a complete treatment of all exceptions or of every later case in the chapter.

textbookImport.basis: Plain-language synthesis of the cited casebook passages; subject to the jurisdictional and source limits stated there.

topics.delegation: A change in who performs is different from a change in who holds a right.
